projects.title: GameBoy WebOS — Retro 8-Bit Handheld Operating System
projects.subtitle: Interactive Web Experience
projects.tagline: A nostalgic 80s cyberpunk & GameBoy-inspired browser Web OS with interactive retro apps.
projects.description: An immersive in-browser web operating system inspired by classic handheld GameBoy consoles and vibrant retro-futuristic cyberpunk aesthetics. Built with animated 3D perspective grids, custom window management, pixel typography, and nostalgic interactive mini-apps.

projects.description: An interactive Formula 1 race replay and telemetry visualization tool built in Python. thoughts.title: Building Trust Through Clear Design & Motion
thoughts.summary: Why purposeful micro-interactions and cognitive clarity convert users better than flashy gimmickry.
content: In high-stakes software, every fraction of a second matters. When a user clicks a button, a subtle 150ms physics-based easing feedback confirms intent without demanding conscious cognitive load.
Clarity isn't just about whitespace; it's about predictable state machines. When animations respect user intent and spatial hierarchy, interfaces feel tangible and reliable.
By removing arbitrary decorative motion and focusing exclusively on meaningful spatial transitions, we build digital products that feel effortless to navigate.

thoughts.title: The Role of Art Direction in Modern SaaS Engineering
thoughts.summary: Bridging the gap between brand identity and component architecture to create unforgettable software.
content: Many modern web applications suffer from template fatigue. When every SaaS app uses the exact same typography, border radius, and color palette, brand memorability drops to zero.

True art direction in web development involves treating the browser as a living canvas: pairing bold editorial typography with precise responsive fluid scaling (`clamp()`), and tailoring the scroll experience to the narrative.
When design tokens and code architecture work in harmony, engineers can ship innovative visual aesthetics without sacrificing maintainability.

thoughts.title: How High-Growth Teams Scale Resilient Design Systems
thoughts.summary: A blueprint for building tokenized component architectures that survive rapid product evolution.
content: A design system should never be a static museum of components. It must be an active, living contract between product designers, engineers, and product managers.
The most resilient systems start with semantic tokens: separating raw color and spacing values from contextual intent (e.g., using `color-surface-hover` rather than hardcoded hex codes).
Investing early in automated visual regression tests and comprehensive documentation saves hundreds of hours of design debt down the road.
